seal.statement: A partition's raft-rs replica-image checkpoint is valid by its own reader. The checkpoint format no longer equates a cluster membership-publication epoch with a per-group Raft membership generation index: that equality is a message-group identity rule and is enforced where message groups define it. Checkpoint creation refuses to report success for an image its own reader rejects. The partition snapshot cadence compacts a user partition's log past the threshold with a production identity (publication epoch >= 1, after a committed membership change), a lagging follower installs the checkpoint through the production dispatch and orchestration, and every cadence or dispatch outcome other than success is logged as a typed outcome. A lagging follower whose snapshot cannot be served is re-asked on a named event or bounded cadence and its stall is visible.

Decision (repair ii, the identity question): the partition identity's epoch author is NOT changed in this quest; the category error is removed and case F is made live with the existing author. What STALE_EPOCH (descriptor epoch >= receiver epoch) protects for partitions: it comes from requirements.md ('A membership-epoch change SHALL abort the transfer') and the S4 design, written when a partition's membership was a control-plane publication and was NOT in the image. Contract-first transition record (solver-quests checklist) for the two changed transitions. (A) Leader re-ask of a follower's snapshot. 1 Producer/consumer symbols: producer raft-rs-peer-delivery.js notifySnapshotCatchupNeeded -> RAFT_OPERATION_PORT_REQUEST.SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_NEEDED (partition-service-raft-init-base.js) -> PartitionService.requestSnapshotCatchupDispatch -> partition-snapshot-catchup-driver.js dispatch -> service.onSnapshotCatchupNeeded (the seam bootstrap/shared/snapshot-catchup-wiring.js attachSnapshotCatchupDispatcher sets) -> snapshot-catchup.js dispatchSnapshotCatchup; the re-ask reads service.raft.readStatus() (peers[].address/addressStatus, followerProgress). 2 Shapes: the decision is snapshot-catchup-constants.js buildSnapshotCatchupDecision unchanged; the dispatch result is the dispatcher's typed result unchanged; the driver's own vocabulary is partition-snapshot-progress-constants.js. 3 Identity/generation: a record is keyed by the decision's followerAddress; it carries the decision's leaderBoundary, the newest generation index and the checkpoint identity key (clusterId + membershipEpoch) observed when its last dispatch settled. 4 Ordering: one dispatch in flight per follower (later notifications coalesce onto it); a sweep never re-asks a record in flight. 5 Absent vs unavailable: no dispatcher wired is the typed dispatcher_unwired; a seam that answers no typed result is dispatch_result_untyped; a thrown seam is dispatch_faulted; an unreadable status is the sweep outcome status_unavailable; a peer whose address the status could not resolve is never read as departed. 6 Durable commit: none; the record is volatile leader state and is rebuilt by raft-rs re-emitting MsgSnapshot after a restart or a new leadership (Progress resets to Probe). 7 Retained obligations: the follower stays in ProgressState::Snapshot until the runtime's existing heartbeat acknowledgement; the driver adds no obligation the runtime does not already hold. 8 Wake and cleanup: wakes are a newer checkpoint generation or a changed identity key (after a dispatch that did not serve) and the declared 30 s bound (PARTITION_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_REASK_BOUND_MS); the record closes when the leader's own progress for the follower is at or past the boundary, the follower left the configuration, or leadership is lost. (B) Cadence refusal: producer snapshot-checkpoint-store.js createSqliteStateMachineCheckpoint (new typed image_rejected, decided by readCheckpoint on the staged image before publication); consumer partition-snapshot-cadence.js; the standing refusal (partition-snapshot-cadence-refusal.js) carries the applied index and identity key of the refused attempt; wakes are applied-index advance or identity change spaced by 1 s doubling to 60 s, and the 60 s bound (PARTITION_SNAPSHOT_CADENCE_RETRY); it is cleared by any attempt that is not refused and by loss of leadership; nothing durable.

Decision (verifier F1): the snapshot transfer contract is ONE BULK CONNECTION PER TRANSFER, closed by the side that dialled it. Chosen over re-arming the offer router on a live connection after reading what shares the connection: the bulk registry keeps one connection per peer node for BOTH directions, and only the adopting side arms an offer router. A reused connection is therefore wrong in every case that can occur once the dialler closes at the end of its dispatch: an open connection to the follower's node can only be that node's own transfer towards this node (its dial, adopted here). An offer sent into it lands on the peer's dialled end, which has no router, and beside another transfer's frames (the serve loop ends on ANY abort frame, whatever its transferId), so re-arming would have needed routers on dialled ends and frame demultiplexing by transfer. Changes: snapshot-catchup.js dispatchSnapshotCatchup closes the channel it was given when the dispatch ends, whatever the outcome (one event-loop turn later so a typed abort it sent is delivered first); snapshot-catchup-wiring.js createBulkSocketProvider always dials, passes the dispatch's signal to the dial, and answers null (typed socket_unavailable) while an open connection to that node exists; snapshot-offer-router.js stays one-shot and answers a typed ABORT to the offering side when it cannot route (new abort reason replica_not_found; chunk_frame_invalid for a first frame that is no offer), so REPLICA_NOT_FOUND and NOT_OFFER no longer leave the leader's serve loop waiting. Both ends followed: abort by the receiver (leader's serve returns the reason, closes); completion (leader closes after COMPLETE); refusal before routing (typed abort, leader closes); receiver silent or dead without a close (the driver's idle bound aborts through the signal: serve answers transfer_cancelled, the dispatch closes the channel and frees the node slot); leader dead without a close (the follower's receive ends when the leader's next dial replaces the connection in the follower's registry, which closes the old one). The finished transfer's listeners end with their connection. The per-node single-flight slot stays; a dispatch that finds it busy answers already_in_flight in its caller's turn and the driver asks again on its next 1 s sweep, so N partitions lagging on one node are served one transfer at a time in the order their sweeps find the slot free (not a fixed order), each waiting at most the transfers ahead of it plus one sweep per hand-over; none waits for ever because a served partition's record leaves the contention. Witnessed with three partitions: all served within two sweeps. Bounds and their reasons (R13): PARTITION_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_DISPATCH_IDLE_BOUND_MS 60 s bounds SILENCE of a dispatch in flight (progress = generation resolved, channel obtained, each chunk served), never a transfer's duration; a seal that outlives it completes, is kept and is served by the next ask. PARTITION_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_SERVED_REASK_BOUND_MS 5 min (verifier F4): a served follower is not offered the image again on the refused bound; a re-offer during an install is in any case the typed replica_not_found refusal (witness R3), because a replica shut down for install is not a running replica. In scope: the transfer contract is the snapshot catch-up of the raft-rs backend, which the quest's epic covers; no supersession needed.
